notes: Also selects the risk-free tenor: the 7y point for a 7-year projection.

growth_rate.source: assumption carried over from the first DCF version, where it was hardcoded; flat explicit growth until growth mean-reversion is modelled

debt_spread.source: assumption carried over from the first DCF version, where it was hardcoded; pre-tax spread over the risk-free rate, no rating-based source wired yet

bank_nii_ratio_threshold.source: assumption: net interest income as a share of total revenue at or above which a company is a bank; a sign test is not usable because the vendor reports a net interest income row for every company (MSFT 0.1%, JPM 52% on yfinance 1.7.0)

terminal_growth_rate.source: per-country long-run nominal growth estimates, June 2026 vintage
notes: The 'default' entry is kept from the original table and is never used as a fallback: a country absent from this table fails the valuation.

unwired._note: Kept verbatim from the original parameter file and not read by the valuation. growth_clamp and mean_reversion belong to a later growth-model change; erp.mode static is the only mode carried forward; rfr_duration is redundant with projection_years, which selects the tenor.

mean_reversion._comment: Mean reversion causes growth rates to decay toward terminal growth. lambda controls speed: 0.1=slow (reaches terminal ~year 10), 0.25=moderate (~year 4), 0.5=fast (~year 2). Set enabled=false for constant growth (legacy behavior).

erp._comment_mode: Options: 'static' (Damodaran, from equity_risk_premiums.json) or 'dynamic' (VIX-adjusted). Dynamic mode fetches current VIX and adjusts base ERP: ERP_dynamic = ERP_base × (VIX/VIX_mean)^sensitivity.
erp._comment_vix: VIX historical mean ~19.5. Sensitivity 0.3-0.5 typical. Higher sensitivity = more reactive to VIX changes. Example: VIX=30, mean=20, sens=0.4 → adjustment=1.18 (18% higher ERP).
